headline: Overnight was quiet as expected. Gutter Gear and Fall Planting are ahead of plan on test-to-date ROAS; Storm Ready Meta is on plan; Nextdoor is below break-even but still too small to judge.
Morning traffic came in on plan. Gutter Gear Search is the strongest line in the test. A smoke advisory for the Ukiah area is expected this afternoon; the agent is watching AQI.

AQI turned unhealthy in the Ukiah area at 1 p.m. The approved Clean Air standby went live there, and Fall Planting outdoor creative paused there. Spend stayed under every cap. Three adjustments are waiting for your approval.
working: Gutter Gear, Google Search: ROAS 4.48 on 714 clicks vs projected base 3.24; 98% chance it's truly above break-even.
Fall Planting, Meta: ROAS 4.95 on 1145 clicks; 99% chance above break-even.
Storm Ready, Meta: ROAS 4.97 in its first 4 days, on plan.
notworking: Storm Ready, Nextdoor: ROAS 1.28 on 61 clicks, below break-even (2.77). Under 100 clicks, so this is early, not a verdict.
Fall Planting, TikTok: only 3.2% of clicks add to cart vs 4.1% on Meta; 62% chance above break-even.
narr.funnel: Biggest leak: Fall Planting TikTok, click to add to cart (3.2% vs 4.1% on Meta). Likely cause: the video sends people to a long blog post on a phone; Meta's top variant links straight to the estimator. Fix: point TikTok to the Garden Soil category with store pickup (ADJ-2).
forces: Ukiah area AQI reached Unhealthy at 1 p.m. (SIMULATED event, modeled on the Oct 16 to 19 Cooley Fire smoke).
NWS: dry through Monday, next rain chance midweek (SIMULATED for Oct 31). Gutter Gear and Storm Ready bursts set to start 48 hours before the next rain.

protective.action: Stock-out pause: Frost King gutter scoop removed from Sonoma ads (0 on hand). Resumes on its own when restocked.

Safety pause: Fall Planting outdoor creative paused in the Ukiah area while AQI is Unhealthy. Resuming needs approval (ADJ-3). The pre-approved Clean Air standby (C5) started in the same area under its approved trigger and caps.

adj.change: Raise Gutter Gear Search daily cap 15% (about $14 a day) for the remaining 10 days, from the reserve.
adj.why: ROAS 4.48 on 714 clicks vs break-even 2.77; 98% chance above break-even.
adj.stage: None: every stage is at or above benchmark. The limit is budget.
adj.diagnosis: Budget-limited, not demand-limited. Ads stop serving by mid-afternoon on rain-forecast days while searches keep coming (simulated: 38% of impressions lost to budget on those days).
causes: Daily cap sized for an average day, but rain days bring two to three times the searches
Strong conversion (above the 3.5% benchmark) means each extra click is likely profitable
remediation: Raise the Search daily cap 15% from the reserve for 10 days
Shift spend toward 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. when pickup is possible
Keep the 48-hour rain bursts; the extra cap only applies on forecast days
Hold the raise at any store where Amerimax gutter guard delivery isn't confirmed by Purchasing
adj.success: ROAS stays above 3.3x (1.2x break-even) and impression share lost to budget falls under 15%.
adj.effect: About $143 more spend; projected extra revenue $500 to $640 at current ROAS.
adj.undo: Return the cap to the approved amount.

adj.change: Point Fall Planting TikTok ads to the Garden Soil category page with store pickup, instead of the blog post, for a 3-day test.
adj.why: Add-to-cart rate 3.2% of clicks vs 4.1% on Meta.
adj.stage: Product view to add to cart (and some loss from click to view).
adj.diagnosis: Landing page mismatch on phones. People tap a short video and land on a long blog post; few scroll to the products, and some leave before it loads.
causes: The blog post is long on a phone; products sit below several screens of how-to
Video viewers expect a shopping page, not an article
Slower page load than the category page (simulated)
remediation: Send TikTok clicks to the Garden Soil category page with store pickup selected
Add on-screen text in the last 3 seconds: 'Pickup today at your Friedman's'
Split 50/50 for 3 days: category page vs the blog post's estimator section
Keep the blog post for Meta, where it converts
adj.success: Add-to-cart rate of 5% or more of clicks, and ROAS above 2.77x after 150 more clicks.
adj.effect: No added spend. If add-to-cart doubles, TikTok ROAS projects above break-even.

adj.success: Ukiah's Fall Planting ROAS returns to within 15% of its pre-pause level within 2 days.

adj.change: Hold Nextdoor at current budget until it passes 100 clicks, then decide. Approve the new store-specific post to test meanwhile.
adj.why: Below break-even, with a 26% chance it's truly above, but on only 61 clicks.
adj.stage: Impression to click, then add to cart to order.
adj.diagnosis: Weak hook and a thin sample. Click rate is about half of Meta's for the same offer, and only 1 order so far, so the data can't separate a bad channel from a bad post.
causes: Generic preparedness copy reads like an ad, not a neighbor's tip
No store name or local detail; Nextdoor rewards local relevance
Too few clicks to judge conversion
remediation: Keep the budget flat; no added spend
Swap in a store-specific post: 'Sandbags are in stock at Friedman's Petaluma' with a fill-and-stack tip (see Ad samples)
Decide at 100 clicks: keep if ROAS is at or above 2.77x, otherwise move the remaining Nextdoor budget to Storm Ready Meta
adj.success: Click rate above 1.3% and ROAS at or above 2.77x by 100 clicks.
